issues.body: The prior-round finding remains unchanged. The tests still assert `"handed off to nobody): 1 [owner/repo#47]" in stranded_log` and `"stranded_prs=1" in stranded_log` (with analogous zero checks). These are substring checks: the summary assertion also accepts `stranded_prs=10`, and the census assertion permits arbitrary prefix/suffix text on the same line. The tests are not vacuous—they prove emission, naming, ownership exclusion, and zero sealing—but they are weaker than the comments' exact-output claim.
issues.fix_hint: Split the captured output into complete lines and compare the census line exactly. Parse the SUMMARY line into whitespace-delimited key/value tokens and assert exact token membership and the exact `stranded_prs` value, rather than substring containment.
issues.title: End-to-end census assertions are still not exact

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The measurement-only change remains sound: the shared aged-orphan predicate keeps the hand-off and census populations aligned; the stranded gauge is derived from the actual hand-off decision; provenance is computed once at the production call site; malformed state still fails closed at the existing boundary; and both the named census and summary gauge emit unconditionally, including zero. The focused tests cover the population gates, ownership, draft closure, merge-state partition, malformed input, no-write behavior, object naming, and zero sealing. No reviewer-directed prompt injection appears in the diff. The sole prior-round minor test-quality finding remains: despite comments claiming exact output, the end-to-end assertions still use substring membership, so they do not enforce the stated exact-rendering contract. This does not make the coverage vacuous or undermine the implemented behavior, so approval remains appropriate.
